sources.entry: Time Machine Inspector - Find out what's hogging up your Time Machine backups. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/probablykasper/time-machine-inspector) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: A Mac app built with Tauri that shows what is taking up space in your Time Machine backups.
summary.what_it_does: Time Machine Inspector is a macOS utility for finding out what is consuming space in Time Machine backups. The README is brief and centers on developer setup rather than feature details. It describes the app as a way to find out what is hogging up your backups and offers a download for Mac. The project is built with Tauri and npm, with scripts for dev mode, building, linting, and formatting. The README also documents a release process that uses CHANGELOG.md, a version bump in src-tauri/Cargo.toml, and a git tag in v#.#.# format. The README does not list specific inspection features beyond the one-line description.
use_cases: Find which folders or files take up the most Time Machine backup space
Figure out why a Time Machine backup disk is filling up
Inspect Mac backup contents to free up storage
Build or modify a Tauri-based macOS desktop app
how_to_run: Run `npm run dev` to start the app in dev mode
notable: Focused purpose: shows what is using up Time Machine backup space
Desktop app built on Tauri with a Rust backend
Includes a documented release workflow using CHANGELOG.md and git tags
Listed in the awesome-mac collection under System Related Tools
caveats: README is short and gives no detail on features, supported macOS versions, or usage
Development requires Node.js, Rust, and the Tauri toolchain setup
